rationale:
Issue #152 (labeled 'bug', closed by PR #153) reports that standard scalars fail on default-value/introspection paths with 'Serialize expected type ID but got Map' and 'Cannot convert value to AST: 0'/'1' for Bool and Int, and explicitly notes Bool worked before 2.10.1, so this is a pre-existing regression rather than a missing feature. The single production file changed, Sources/GraphQL/Type/Scalars.swift, replaces the uniformly lossy 'serialize: { try map(from: $0) }' and 'parseValue: { try .x($0.xValue(converting: true)) }' closures on GraphQLInt/Float/String/Boolean/ID with explicit coercion that accepts Map-wrapped inputs (e.g. GraphQLID.serialize now returns .string for Map .string/.number), which is the direct cause of the reported 'got Map' failure. All five retained hunks are the same edit applied to the five built-in scalars; the only added declarations are the internal GRAPHQL_MAX_INT/GRAPHQL_MIN_INT bounds used by the new Int coercion, and their doc comments are part of that added code, not a documentation-only change. There is no formatting-only, config, or test change in the minimized production patch (retained 5 of 5, removed 0, post_minimization_validation PASS). The triggers are the unmodified test file from the same fixing commit and exercise only pre-existing members (GraphQLInt/Float/String/Boolean/ID .serialize and .parseValue) with literal Map fixtures; they do not reference GRAPHQL_MAX_INT/GRAPHQL_MIN_INT or any new production API, and strict evidence confirms they compile and fail at afbad07 and pass at 2a17bfc. Machine strict gates pass on both the original and post-minimization matrices: build.both_versions, selectors.present_and_unique (10/10), trigger.buggy_differential with all 10 selectors reproduced, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (12/12 fingerprint groups), full_suite.fixed_all_green, and full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, at 3 repetitions over 86 runs. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #152 is not a duplicate, and it is the sole entry in allowed_root_cause_ids.

Issue #152 (labeled 'bug', closed by this work) reports that introspection of default values fails with 'Serialize expected type ID but got Map', 'Cannot convert value to AST: 0' for Bool, and 'Cannot convert value to AST: 1' for Int, and notes Bool worked before 2.10.1, so this is a pre-existing regression in built-in scalar coercion rather than a missing feature. The fix commit 2a17bfc replaces the uniform `serialize: { try map(from: $0) }` and lossy `parseValue` closures in Sources/GraphQL/Type/Scalars.swift with explicit case handling that accepts Map-wrapped inputs (GraphQLID now returns .string for both .string and .number Map cases; GraphQLBoolean handles .bool/.number Map cases; GraphQLInt handles .number), directly addressing the reported failure mode. Commit message and PR #153 both state 'Fixes .../issues/152', and traceability records path fix_commit_to_issue with verified issue 152. Scope: exactly one production file, five hunks, all in the same serialize/parseValue coercion logic for the five built-in scalars. The only added declarations are internal constants GRAPHQL_MAX_INT/GRAPHQL_MIN_INT, consumed by the changed Int logic, so no public API extension, no formatting-only, docs-only, config-only, or test-only content in the production patch. Automatic minimization retained all 5 of 5 hunks with post_minimization_validation PASS, consistent with the ten triggers spanning all five scalars in both directions. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test file Tests/GraphQLTests/TypeTests/ScalarTests.swift from the same single fixing commit (not curator-written, not from a later commit), and it exercises only pre-existing members (GraphQLInt/Float/String/Boolean/ID .serialize and .parseValue) that exist at parent afbad07, so it does not depend on any API introduced by the fix; strict evidence confirms build.both_versions passed and all ten selectors compiled and reproduced on the buggy revision. Machine-generated strict gates pass in both the original and post-minimization matrices: trigger.buggy_differential, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (12/12 fingerprint groups), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, full_suite.fixed_all_green, matrix.complete (86 runs), 3 repetitions, zero failed checks. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #152 is not a duplicate, and it matches the single allowed_root_cause_ids entry.

risks: The fix is broader than the three scalars named in the issue: Float and String coercion, and stricter parseValue rejection (Int rejecting "123", Boolean rejecting 0/1, String rejecting numbers), are included. These share the single root cause (blanket map(from:)/converting coercion) but the trigger set asserts behavior beyond the exact symptoms reported.

The new Int serialize branch throws a message reading 'Float cannot represent non numeric value' for non-number Map inputs, a copy-paste defect carried into the fixed revision; it does not affect the differential outcome but leaves an incorrect diagnostic string in the accepted fixed state.

The upstream test file contains commented-out TODO assertions and expected-message strings ported from graphql-js that do not always match the messages this implementation throws, so the differential signal rests on throw/no-throw and value equality rather than message text.
All 10 declared selectors live in one new file, so the case offers no independent trigger outside ScalarTests.swift.
issue_evidence is null; the issue text was read from source_candidate.issue_check.linked_issues rather than a dedicated fetched-issue record.
